column1: # Cases for open-away-stretch.sh — one per line, tab-separated:
#   name  pre  prompt  want  stretch_after
# pre:           none | open   (a stretch the runner opens, until 09:00, before the prompt)
# want:          open (stretch opened: systemMessage + additionalContext) | closed | no-stretch | error (decision block) | silent
# stretch_after: open | not-open | none   (what `away-obligation status` says for the session afterwards)
# The runner sets the clock to 2026-10-20 03:00 local; \n in a prompt is decoded.
until a time opens a stretch
until a time, with the user's words
column3: /away until 09:00 keep my machine idle and then carry on

column1: for a duration opens a stretch
for minutes
for hours and minutes
more than 12 hours is capped, not refused
a time already past today means tomorrow
a second /away replaces the first
bare /away is an error
bare /away leaves an open stretch alone
until with no value is an error
unknown word is an error
a bad time is an error
a bad duration is an error
off closes an open stretch
off with no stretch open
a typed prompt that is not /away leaves the stretch open
/away inside a sentence is silent
a longer word is silent
a task notification leaves the stretch open
a wakeup prompt leaves the stretch open
column3: Check the filed job and report.
